schema_query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

columns.name: judge_name
columns.definition: The full name of the federal judge presiding over the case.
columns.rationale: Required to identify the specific judge and link them to their appointing President.

columns.name: appointing_president
columns.definition: The name of the U.S. President who appointed the judge to the federal bench.
columns.rationale: Directly addresses the core query comparing Trump appointees, other Republican appointees, and Democratic appointees.

columns.name: appointing_president_party
columns.definition: The political party of the President who appointed the judge.
columns.rationale: Enables grouping and comparison of voting tendencies between Republican and Democratic appointees.

columns.name: case_outcome_immigration_supportive
columns.definition: Indicates whether the judge's ruling or vote supported the immigration policy/action of the presidential administration in power at the time of the lawsuit.
columns.rationale: Directly answers whether Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration policies compared to other judges.

columns.name: injunction_ruling_type
columns.definition: The court's decision regarding the requested immigration injunction.
columns.rationale: Captures the specific voting/ruling tendency on the injunction request.
allowed_values: granted in part and denied in part

columns.name: challenged_administration
columns.definition: The presidential administration whose immigration policy or action is being challenged in the case.
columns.rationale: Allows researchers to isolate cases challenging Trump administration policies versus other administrations.
